gloss: to breathe a sigh of relief; to feel relieved

definitions.gloss: to breathe a sigh of relief; to feel relieved
definitions.explanation: An idiomatic expression meaning to feel greatly relieved after a period of anxiety or worry. Literally, 'to stroke one's chest downward' — a gesture of relief.

examples.japanese: ⟦{無事|ぶじ}→無事：01602_buji⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{聞|き}いて→聞く：00483_kiku⟧{胸|むね}をなでおろした。
examples.english: I breathed a sigh of relief when I heard everyone was safe.

examples.japanese: ⟦{試験|しけん}→試験：01422_shiken⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合格|ごうかく}して→合格する：27949_goukakusuru⟧、⟦やっと→やっと：01561_yatto⟧{胸|むね}をなでおろすこと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: I finally felt relieved after passing the exam.

examples.japanese: ⟦{手術|しゅじゅつ}→手術：03218_shujutsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{成功|せいこう}した→成功する：21445_seikousuru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{医者|いしゃ}→医者：02847_isha⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{聞|き}いて→聞く：00483_kiku⟧、⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦{全員|ぜんいん}→全員：03310_zenin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{胸|むね}をなでおろした。
examples.english: The whole family breathed a sigh of relief when the doctor said the surgery was successful.

notes:
USAGE:
The literal image is of stroking one's chest downward as a physical expression of relief, a gesture seen in Japanese culture when tension subsides. Almost always used in the past tense ({胸|むね}をなでおろした) to describe the moment relief is felt. Can also be written with kanji as ⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{撫|な}で{下|お}ろす→撫で下ろす：07099_nadeorosu⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{無事|ぶじ}→無事：01602_buji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}いて→聞く：00483_kiku⟧{胸|むね}をなでおろす (to feel relieved upon hearing someone is safe)
- ⟦やっと→やっと：01561_yatto⟧{胸|むね}をなでおろす (to finally feel relieved)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ほっとする→ほっとする：07652_hottosuru⟧: to feel relieved — simpler, more casual expression
- ⟦{安堵|あんど}する→安堵する：15624_andosuru⟧: to feel relieved — more formal, literary alternative
